name: AWS New Carlisle data center campus (Project Rainier)
summary: Amazon Web Services campus in the Indiana Enterprise Center near New Carlisle, St. Joseph County, announced in April 2024 as an $11 billion build over roughly a decade. It is one of the sites of Project Rainier, the Trainium2 cluster Anthropic uses to build and deploy Claude, which AWS activated in October 2025. Amazon's utility filings describe a 2,250 MW load. In July 2026 AWS said it had invested $13.8 billion, with about 18 of a planned 30 or so buildings running and construction continuing.

location.note: Sources place the campus in the Indiana Enterprise Center near New Carlisle but give no parcel or address; coordinates are the New Carlisle town point from its Wikipedia article (Nominatim was unavailable).

parties.name: Anthropic
parties.note: Amazon says Anthropic uses Project Rainier, which spans several US data centers including this one, to build and deploy Claude; trade press says the site's chips are dedicated to Anthropic's models.

Trade press reported AWS's activation of Project Rainier on 29 October 2025, with seven buildings at this site complete and in use; Amazon called the cluster fully operational. Earlier partial use is not dated in the sources.
Campus administration building opened, housing workforce development programs.

power_sources.description: Served by Indiana Michigan Power, which expects new data center load to double its demand by 2030; a consumer group says the utility has proposed adding gas-fired generation.
